entries.overview: A nimble muscular organ anchored to the floor of the mouth and covered by taste-sensing papillae.
entries.function: Shapes sounds for speech, detects taste, and pushes chewed food backward into the throat to swallow.

facts: Contains both intrinsic muscles that change its shape and extrinsic muscles that shift its position.
Papillae on its upper surface grip food and house clusters of taste buds.

sources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — The Tongue

entries.overview: A collapsible muscular tube about 25 cm long traveling behind the windpipe through the chest to the abdomen.
entries.function: Propels swallowed food and liquids down into the stomach using coordinated muscular waves (peristalsis).

facts: Passes through a small muscular opening in the diaphragm right above the stomach.
Guarded at top and bottom by muscular sphincters that help prevent stomach acid reflux.

sources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — The Esophagus

entries.overview: A J-shaped muscular pouch tucked beneath the left ribcage between the esophagus and small intestine.
entries.function: Stores eaten meals, churns food into acidic liquid chyme, and starts breaking down dietary protein.

facts: Folds called rugae allow the empty stomach to expand smoothly after a large meal.
Gastric glands secrete hydrochloric acid and the protein-digesting enzyme pepsin while mucus protects the lining.

sources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Structure of the Stomach

entries.overview: The largest internal gland in the body, wedged beneath the right diaphragm under the lower ribs.
entries.function: Processes nutrients from the gut, makes bile for fat digestion, detoxifies blood, and builds vital plasma proteins.

facts: Receives dual blood flow from the oxygen-rich hepatic artery and the nutrient-rich hepatic portal vein.
Stores excess glucose as glycogen and releases it back into the bloodstream between meals.
Can regenerate lost tissue after injury faster than almost any other solid organ.

sources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — The Liver

entries.overview: A small pear-shaped green sac nestled into a shallow hollow on the underside of the liver.
entries.function: Stores and concentrates liver-made bile, squeezing it into the small intestine when fatty food arrives.

facts: Holds roughly 30 to 60 milliliters of concentrated bile between meals.
Connects via the cystic duct to the common bile duct emptying into the duodenum.

sources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — The Gallbladder

entries.overview: A soft, elongated gland lying horizontally behind the stomach with its head cradled in the curve of the duodenum.
entries.function: Releases digestive enzymes into the small intestine and secretes insulin and glucagon to steady blood sugar.

facts: Works as both an exocrine digestive gland and an endocrine hormone gland.
Produces bicarbonate-rich fluid to neutralize stomach acid entering the small intestine.

sources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — The Pancreas

entries.overview: The short C-shaped first loop of the small intestine curving around the head of the pancreas.
entries.function: Neutralizes stomach acid and mixes chyme with bile and pancreatic enzymes to complete chemical digestion.

facts: Measures about 25 cm (roughly twelve finger-widths) long.
Serves as a primary site for absorbing dietary iron and neutralizing gastric acid.

sources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — The Small and Large Intestines

entries.overview: The coiled middle section of the small intestine filling the upper left and central abdomen.
entries.function: Absorbs most digested sugars, amino acids, and fats across millions of microscopic finger-like villi.

facts: Has taller circular folds and denser blood supply than the ileum, maximizing nutrient uptake.
Makes up roughly two-fifths of the small intestine between the duodenum and ileum.

sources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — The Small and Large Intestines

entries.overview: The first vertical segment of the large intestine rising along the right side of the abdomen up to the liver.
entries.function: Absorbs remaining water and salts from undigested residue as material moves upward toward the transverse colon.

facts: Begins above the cecum near the right hip and bends sharply under the liver at the right colic flexure.
Anchored against the back abdominal wall so it stays in place during digestion.

sources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Large Intestine Anatomy
